items.abstract: <jats:p>With the rapid growth of multimodal data on e-commerce platforms and social media, accurately determining whether different text-image records refer to the same real-world entity has become a key research problem. However, existing work predominantly focuses on text-only entity matching, leaving multimodal entity matching (MEM) relatively underexplored. While recent large vision-language models (VLMs) provide strong cross-modal understanding, they are not directly suitable for MEM because they are trained for generation rather than discriminative matching, and they are sensitive to noisy or incomplete text-image records. To address these limitations, we propose VLM-Match, a discriminative VLM-based framework for MEM. First, we introduce a high-confidence positive-pair data augmentation strategy with dual consistency constraints to alleviate positive-pair scarcity. Second, we extract verifiable entity evidence for semantic completion and propose a Region Localization and Semantic Alignment (RLSA) module for text-region alignment while suppressing background noise. Finally, we introduce a unified discriminative training objective that combines classification and contrastive learning for fine-grained multimodal matching. Experiments on eight real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of VLM-Match, achieving an average F1 improvement of 10.4% over the best baseline.</jats:p>
title: Towards Entity-Discriminative Large Vision-Language Models for Multimodal Entity Matching

items.abstract: <jats:p>Named entity matching plays a critical role in data integration tasks, where the challenge lies in accurately identifying and linking records that refer to the same real-world entities across disparate data sources. The novel integration of Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) for optimizing hyperparameter tuning in fine-tuning language models, such as Mistral, presents a significant advancement in enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of entity matching. The research focuses on leveraging Mistral LLM to identify subtle variations in ransomware-related entities, showcasing the effectiveness of MCTS in systematically exploring the hyperparameter space to achieve optimal model configurations. Extensive experimentation demonstrated the superiority of the fine-tuned model over traditional approaches, including rule-based systems and support vector machines, in terms of precision, recall, and F1-score. The study also involved a detailed error analysis and sensitivity analysis, highlighting the critical impact of hyperparameter selection on model performance and the ability of MCTS to streamline the optimization process. The findings provide valuable insights into the potential of combining advanced search techniques with language models to address complex entity matching tasks in various domains.</jats:p>
title: A Novel Approach to Optimize Large Language Models for Named Entity Matching with Monte Carlo Tree Search
